name: YouTube Video Platform
description: Design YouTube's video upload and streaming platform. Covers video transcoding pipeline, CDN delivery, search indexing, and content metadata management at massive scale.

learnSteps.title: Video Upload Pipeline
learnSteps.description: When a creator uploads a video, the API Service stores the raw file in object storage and publishes a transcode job to Kafka. The transcoding pipeline (using FFmpeg) generates multiple resolutions (144p to 4K) and formats (H.264, VP9, AV1). Each resolution is split into small chunks for adaptive bitrate streaming.

learnSteps.title: Video Viewing via CDN
learnSteps.description: Viewers stream videos from the nearest CDN edge location. The CDN caches popular video chunks (the top 20% of videos get 80% of views). On a cache miss, the CDN pulls from origin object storage. Adaptive bitrate streaming (DASH/HLS) dynamically switches quality based on the viewer's bandwidth.

learnSteps.title: Search and Discovery
learnSteps.description: Video metadata (title, description, tags, auto-generated captions) is indexed in Elasticsearch. The search engine supports fuzzy matching, relevance scoring (combining text relevance, view count, freshness, and user preferences), and autocomplete suggestions.

learnSteps.title: Metadata and Caching Layer
learnSteps.description: Video metadata (view counts, likes, channel info) is stored in sharded MySQL. Redis caches hot metadata — trending videos, popular channels, and session data. With billions of daily views, the cache-aside pattern reduces database load by over 90%. View counts use approximate counters to avoid write contention.

chaosScenarios.name: Continental CDN Degradation at Peak
chaosScenarios.description: An edge software rollout degrades a continent's PoP tier during evening peak, pushing a tenth of global watch traffic onto remaining regions and origin
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Affected viewers re-steer to distant PoPs: video start time doubles, ABR players drop 1-2 bitrate tiers. Hit rate on receiving PoPs falls as a cold working set arrives. Origin read amplification grows until edge caches re-warm — origin egress is the metric to watch, not edge error rate.
mitigationSteps: Halt the edge rollout and roll back — config/rollout is the first suspect in fleet-wide edge incidents
Steer traffic via anycast withdrawal and watch receiving-region utilization for cascade
Cap the top bitrate tier in affected regions to cut bytes per stream ~40%
Enable origin shield to collapse duplicate cache-fill fetches per segment

chaosScenarios.name: MySQL Primary Failover Under Write Load
chaosScenarios.description: The metadata primary crashes during peak upload hours; a replica must be promoted while view-count and metadata writes queue
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Writes fail for 30-60s during promotion. Reads continue from replicas and the 92%-hit cache, so watching and browsing barely degrade. Replicas with replication lag serve slightly stale view counts. Queued counter increments flush after promotion, causing a visible count jump.
mitigationSteps: Verify automated promotion selected the least-lagged replica
Fence the old primary before it can accept writes on recovery (split-brain prevention)
Flush buffered counter increments in batches to avoid a write stampede on the new primary
Audit replication topology before declaring all-clear

chaosScenarios.name: Elasticsearch Shard Reallocation Storm
chaosScenarios.description: Two search data nodes fail, triggering mass shard recovery that saturates cluster I/O while search queries continue arriving
chaosScenarios.expectedBehavior: Search latency rises 10x as recovery I/O competes with queries; some shards go unassigned, returning partial results. Watch and browse paths are unaffected — search is an isolated failure domain. Indexing of new uploads backs up.
mitigationSteps: Throttle shard recovery concurrency and bandwidth so queries keep breathing room
Serve degraded results: cached trending/popular fallback for failed query shards
Pause non-urgent reindexing jobs until cluster returns to green
Replace failed nodes; let allocation awareness rebuild across zones

bottleneckProgression.description: Hot metadata working set outgrows 256GB; eviction rate climbs and misses leak to MySQL
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Shard the Redis cluster wider and pin trending-page keys with longer TTLs

bottleneckProgression.description: View-count write contention on viral video rows saturates the MySQL primary
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Sharded approximate counters aggregated in batches; move counters off the relational primary

bottleneckProgression.description: Video API fleet saturates on session, manifest, and recommendation fan-out
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Scale the fleet; precompute home-feed candidates per user cohort offline

bottleneckProgression.description: Edge egress approaches PoP port capacity in dense metros at synchronized peak
bottleneckProgression.resolution: Add PoP capacity and deepen ISP-embedded caches; shift encoding mix toward AV1 to cut bytes per stream

expectedIssues.title: View-Count Hotspot on Viral Videos
expectedIssues.description: A video going viral concentrates millions of increments per minute on one MySQL row; lock contention stalls the write path far below aggregate capacity
expectedIssues.mitigation: Approximate sharded counters buffered in the cache tier, flushed to MySQL in periodic aggregated batches

expectedIssues.title: Trending-Key Cache Stampede
expectedIssues.description: Trending and home-row cache keys expire under massive concurrent demand; thousands of identical queries race to MySQL in the regeneration window
expectedIssues.mitigation: Jittered TTLs, stale-while-revalidate serving, and single-flight regeneration locks per key

expectedIssues.title: Transcode Backlog During Upload Spikes
expectedIssues.description: Breaking-news upload surges outpace the 200-way transcoder; Kafka absorbs the backlog but time-to-publish stretches from minutes to hours
expectedIssues.mitigation: Scale transcoder parallelism on consumer lag; publish low-res renditions first and backfill quality tiers

expectedIssues.title: Search Index Freshness Lag
expectedIssues.description: New uploads are watchable via direct link minutes before they are searchable, because Elasticsearch indexing trails the metadata write path
expectedIssues.mitigation: Track indexing lag as an SLO; fast-path index of title/channel fields ahead of full enrichment (captions, topics)

expectedIssues.title: Long-Tail Origin Read Amplification
expectedIssues.description: The 10% of requests for unpopular videos miss at 300 independent PoPs, each filling separately from origin — the same cold video can be fetched hundreds of times
expectedIssues.mitigation: Hierarchical caching: regional mid-tier caches between PoPs and origin collapse duplicate fills

steps: Check for in-flight edge rollouts first and roll back before deeper diagnosis
Confirm scope via per-PoP TTFF and hit-rate panels
Steer traffic away from degraded PoPs; watch receiving-region load
Cap top bitrate tier regionally if origin egress climbs past safe headroom
Re-warm recovered PoPs before returning them to full rotation
Confirm automated promotion completed and the old primary is fenced
Verify cache hit rate is absorbing reads while replicas catch up
Flush buffered view-count increments in rate-limited batches
Run a replication topology audit before closing the incident
Enable trending/popular fallback results for failing query shards
Throttle shard recovery so query latency stays bounded
Pause bulk reindex jobs; let upload indexing lag rather than fail
Replace lost nodes and verify zone-aware shard placement on recovery

decisions.title: Watch Path and API Path Are Separate Systems
decisions.context: Video bytes dwarf metadata bytes by orders of magnitude; coupling them means the API tier must scale with egress
decisions.decision: Clients stream segments directly from CDN edges; the load-balanced API fleet handles only browse, search, upload, and session traffic
consequences: An API-tier incident never interrupts in-progress playback
CDN capacity planning is decoupled from compute planning
Per-view authorization relies on signed segment URLs rather than inline checks

decisions.title: Kafka-Decoupled Transcode Pipeline
decisions.context: Upload bursts (news events) exceed any fixed transcoder fleet, and transcoding tolerates minutes of latency
decisions.decision: Buffer all upload jobs in a 256-partition Kafka topic consumed by a 200-way FFmpeg pipeline that scales on consumer lag
consequences: Upload acceptance is never throttled by transcode capacity
Backlog converts surges into publish-time delay instead of failures
Consumer lag becomes the canonical pipeline health signal

decisions.title: Approximate Counters for View Counts
decisions.context: Billions of daily views concentrated on popular videos make exact per-row increments a lock-contention disaster
decisions.decision: Buffer increments in sharded cache-tier counters and flush aggregated deltas to MySQL periodically
consequences: Write path scales with cache throughput, not row-lock throughput
Displayed counts are approximate and briefly stale by design
Counter reconciliation jobs become part of the data platform

tradeoffs.benefit: Viral videos cannot stall the metadata write path
tradeoffs.cost: Counts lag reality by seconds-to-minutes and jump visibly when batches flush

tradeoffs.choice: Full rendition ladder (144p-4K, H.264/VP9/AV1) per video
tradeoffs.benefit: Optimal stream for every device and connection; modern codecs cut egress meaningfully at this scale
tradeoffs.cost: Storage multiplies per codec; 10PB is dominated by renditions of rarely-watched videos

tradeoffs.choice: Asynchronous Elasticsearch indexing decoupled from the upload transaction
tradeoffs.benefit: Uploads never block on the search cluster, which can degrade independently
tradeoffs.cost: A freshness window where new videos are watchable but not searchable

alternatives.name: Exact Transactional View Counts
alternatives.description: Increment the video row inside each playback transaction
alternatives.prosVsCons: Perfectly accurate counts and zero reconciliation machinery, but single-row lock contention caps any viral video at the row's lock throughput
alternatives.whyNotChosen: The hottest videos are precisely the ones that would break it; approximate counts are an accepted product norm

alternatives.name: NoSQL Metadata Store
alternatives.description: Replace sharded MySQL with a wide-column store (Bigtable/Cassandra-style) for metadata
alternatives.prosVsCons: Native horizontal write scaling, but loses relational queries, secondary indexes, and transactional semantics that channel/playlist features rely on
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Vitess-style sharded MySQL keeps SQL semantics while scaling writes; the migration risk outweighs the benefit

alternatives.name: Synchronous Search Indexing
alternatives.description: Index into Elasticsearch within the upload request so videos are instantly searchable
alternatives.prosVsCons: Zero freshness lag, but couples upload availability to search cluster health and slows every upload by indexing latency
alternatives.whyNotChosen: Search is the least availability-critical path; letting it lag is strictly better than letting it block uploads
